sources.title: Montana Employer and Information Agent Guide with Tax Tables

calculation.formula: W = A + B * (G - C), where G is gross earnings for the payroll period; then add requested extra withholding.
calculation.periodThresholdDerivation: The guide publishes direct Daily, Weekly, Biweekly, Semimonthly, Monthly, and Annual A/B/C tables for each filing-status group. Annual schedules above preserve the complete rate structure; direct period tables remain authoritative where division creates rounded thresholds or bases.

supplementalWages.combined: Calculate from total regular and supplemental wages.
separatelyPaidMethods: Aggregate with regular wages for the current payroll period
Aggregate with regular wages for the last preceding payroll period in the same calendar year

residencyAndWorkRules.generalRule: Withhold from wages for services performed in Montana unless a federal or Montana exemption applies.
residencyAndWorkRules.northDakotaReciprocity: A North Dakota resident is exempt from Montana wage tax after completing Form MW-4 line 5.

excludedWorkers: Key employee whose prior-year salary exceeded $500,000

residencyAndWorkRules.transitionRule: If the employee is expected to exceed 30 Montana workdays, works only in Montana, or has other Montana-source income, begin withholding when Montana work begins rather than waiting for day 31.
residencyAndWorkRules.nativeReservationExemption: An enrolled tribal member must both reside on and earn the wages on the reservation governed by that tribe; mixed wages and residence periods require allocation.
residencyAndWorkRules.interstateMotorAndRailCarrierRule: Withhold only in the employee's state of residence.

filing.lookbackPeriod: July 1 of the preceding year through June 30 of the current year
filing.newBusinesses: Monthly until an initial lookback period is complete.
filing.exemptMW4Submission: Submit new or updated exemption Forms MW-4 through TAP by the last day of the payroll period in which received; renew annually by January 31.

captureWarnings: The annual schedules preserve every rate and annual threshold, but the official direct payroll-period tables remain necessary for exact A and C values because the agency rounds period thresholds and base amounts.
The 30-day exemption is prospective and category-sensitive; a single elapsed-day counter is insufficient.
Native-reservation exemption requires both residence and work-source facts that can change within a pay period.

review.requiredNextStep: Import all direct period tables, implement required ceiling rounding and prospective 30-day/reservation state, then add example, threshold, reciprocity, and special-worker regression tests.
